transcript.content: Hi, welcome in, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m having a hard time staying locked in on things I need to pay attention to. Like at work, I’ll start a safety briefing or go over a plan and I’m really trying to focus, but a few minutes in my mind is already off on three other job problems. Then I miss stuff I know I should’ve caught.
Have you had this kind of trouble focusing since you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently?

No, it goes way back. Even in elementary school, teachers were telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, I’d talk out of turn, lose homework, and rush through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do.
Aside from getting distracted, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about multiple things—more than the situation seems to call for—on most days?

I don’t know that I’d call it excessive worrying. I mean, I’ve got normal stress with work and family stuff, but I haven’t really noticed myself worrying about a bunch of things most days more than makes sense.
